subject: Action: Finalize customer-facing IP path & training blackout windows
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@halcyon.com>

Cc: Halcyon Legal <legal@halcyon.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines: Order Form IP & training prohibition

Marissa — thanks for taking this on. Attached are Halcyon's current redlines to the Order Form and the related excerpt from our MSA (see Halcyon_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). High level asks from legal/procurement: 

1) Output ownership: Halcyon is asking for explicit assignment of customer outputs generated by the service for the customer’s internal and commercial use (we have highlighted suggested language).
2) Training / retraining: we want a firm prohibition on using any Halcyon data (including prompts, uploaded files, and outputs) to train or update Redwood models for 3 years, unless Halcyon provides explicit written consent.
3) Feedback license: Halcyon requests that any feedback or telemetry Redwood uses for model improvement be strictly aggregated and not attributable to Halcyon, and only with opt-in at the account level.

Can you confirm Redwood’s position on (1) assignment of outputs, (2) the 3-year training ban, and (3) the feedback/telemetry opt-in? Procurement is hoping to close this week; they asked for text they can drop into the Order Form.

Attachments: Halcyon_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (PDF, 1 page redline)

Thanks — Emily

Subject: Re: Initial redlines: Order Form IP & training prohibition

Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. I pulled the attachments into our ticket and started a short internal review. High level — we want to get this done this week, and we think a compromise will get both parties comfortable: 

- Output rights: Redwood can grant Halcyon a perpetual, royalty-free right to use Outputs produced for Halcyon (internal & external commercial use) but we need to limit assignment scope to defined deliverables / catalogued outputs (so we avoid blanket assignment of model improvements). Happy to provide redline language that defines "Outputs" and carves out model IP.

- Training / retraining: a flat 3-year global ban is challenging operationally (there are telemetry and reliability use cases). Proposal: prohibit model retraining on identifiable Halcyon data without express written consent for 24 months; allow usage of aggregated + de-identified telemetry for system reliability (not model training for product improvement) and explicitly exclude telemetry from retraining unless opted in.

- Feedback license: we can agree to an aggregated, non-attributable feedback license and offer an account-level opt-out. For commercial improvements (i.e., training for product models), Redwood would require an explicit opt-in and an additional commercial terms discussion.

I've attached a short redlines_summary.xlsx with suggested compromise text and asked Ben (contracts) and Irene (privacy/ops) to weigh in on specific wording. Proposed next steps: 

1) Internal sync (legal + product + account) — I can host a 30-min call today at 4pm PT.
2) I'll send a proposed Order Form v4 for Halcyon's review by tomorrow EOD.

Can Procurement confirm whether Halcyon is open to the 24-month window and the account-level opt-out for feedback? If yes, we can circulate text and close via DocuSign.

Attachments: redlines_summary.xlsx (Excel, 2 sheets)

Thanks,

Marissa / Irene — quick take from contracts/privacy: 

1) Outputs: suggested clause (drop-in): 
"Customer Outputs": "Customer Outputs" means text, files or other content generated by the Service in response to Customer inputs. Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable right to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute Customer Outputs solely as set forth in the Order Form; provided, however, that Customer Outputs do not include any Model Weights, Model Architectures, or other Proprietary Model Components of Redwood.

2) Training prohibition: replace '3 years' with '24 months' but add narrow exceptions: 
- Redwood will not use Customer Inputs, Uploaded Data, or Customer Outputs to train or improve production models for commercial productization for 24 months without Customer's prior written consent. 
- Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for reliability and safety improvements (not for model training that influences product behavior) unless Customer opts in to broader usage.

3) Feedback license: proposed wording: non-exclusive, perpetual (for the limited purpose of diagnosing and improving the Service), worldwide, royalty-free license to use Customer's feedback in aggregated, de-identified form; opt-out available at the account level. For any training intended to incorporate Customer Data into product models, Redwood will seek separate agreement and compensation.

I also recommend adding an explicit definition of "Aggregated, De-identified" to avoid ambiguity, and a 30-day notice period for changes to telemetry practices. 

I'll prepare a tracked-redline of OrderForm v4 with the insertion points and upload to the deal HubSpot record. If Procurement needs a single drop-in paragraph for DocuSign, we can provide that.

Ben Carter

Subject: RE: Initial redlines: Order Form IP & training prohibition — proposed compromise

Emily / Halcyon team — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. After consulting product, privacy, and legal, please find our proposed compromise summarized below and attached (OrderForm_v4_proposed.pdf). If Halcyon can confirm acceptance of these points, we can update the Order Form and route for signatures. 

Summary of proposed terms (high level):

- Outputs: Redwood will grant Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free right to use Outputs produced for Customer, including commercial use, subject to the Order Form. We will not assign Redwood's underlying model IP (weights, architectures, training data). Where Customer requires assignment, we can discuss this for specific deliverables and include a schedule of assigned deliverables in the Order Form.

- Training / retraining blackout: Redwood will not use Customer Inputs, Uploaded Data, or Customer Outputs to train or improve Redwood production models for 24 months without Customer's prior written consent. Exception: aggregated, de-identified telemetry may be used for service reliability and safety (explicitly excluded from "training for product improvement"). If Halcyon elects to opt into training (earlier than 24 months), we will require a separate agreement that includes commercial terms.

- Feedback license: Redwood requests a non-exclusive license to use Customer feedback and telemetry in aggregated, de-identified form for the purpose of diagnosing, maintaining, and improving the Service. This license will exclude any use that would result in direct incorporation of identifiable Customer data into product models without separate written consent. An account-level opt-out will be available and documented in the Order Form.

- Governance and evidence: Redwood will add definitions for "Aggregated, De-identified" and "Customer Outputs" and include a 30-day notice for changes to telemetry practices. We will provide a short evidence package (audit logs and data flow diagram) to Halcyon's security team on request.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Halcyon to confirm if 24 months + opt-out for feedback is acceptable.
2) If yes, Redwood will circulate OrderForm_v4_proposed.pdf (attached) and a single paragraph for DocuSign insertion.
3) If Halcyon requests 36 months or assignment language for all outputs, we'll need to escalate to commercial leadership to consider concession items.

Attachments: OrderForm_v4_proposed.pdf (PDF, 3 pages — highlighted changes)

Please let me know by EOD Wednesday 5/15 so Procurement can close the DocuSign. Happy to jump on a 15-min call to walk the text.

Best,
